summary:
The trends category is the story of the month — all four ratings sit at identical 30-16 (65%, n=46) over the last 14 days against a 56-59% season baseline, every one of them flagged HOT and riding a 3W streak. SP is right behind it, with R1/R2 both at 28-18 (61%, n=46, HOT +7.8pts) and a 4W streak across the board. The one category to actively fade right now is bullpen_fatigue, cold across all four ratings at an identical 17-29 (37%, n=46), a 9-point drop from season form — any pick leaning on that input deserves a discount today. R4's hitting number is the standout anomaly of the slate: 30-16 (65%, +13.3pts over season) on a 9-game win streak, the hottest single cell in the model.

Today's two-game board is about as clean as it gets — full consensus on both sides. All four ratings back LAD over ATL, with R3 showing the largest edge at +2.03 and the group clustering tightly between +1.84 and +1.90 elsewhere; that kind of unanimous, high-delta alignment is exactly where trends+sp combos (58.1%, 362-261 season) have hit best, and LAD as a liked team has been money all year at 37-15 (71%, n=52) with a strong-play mark of 27-6 (82%, +27.0u) — the best team-trust number on the board. The SDP @ MIL side is also consensus-four-for-four on MIL, but the deltas are soft (+0.32 to +0.59), nowhere near the conviction level of the LAD game — treat this as a lean, not a lock. MIL's season profile as a liked team is strong too (42-22, 66%, strong 26-12 +17.0u), so there's real backing if you want in, but with trends and SP both running hot league-wide and bullpen_fatigue cold, the LAD game is where those hot signals and the biggest model gap intersect — that's the top play of the day.
